one_liner: Pre-1.0 Zig EVM with tail-call dispatch; first-party runs beat evmone baseline and revm on storage and snailtracer fixtures.
what_it_does: evmz is an Ethereum execution engine (interpreter, transaction program, block state transition and stateless witness validation) written in Zig, with the fork specification bound at compile time (evmz.Vm(evmz.eth.cancun), Spec.extend for custom forks). It is consumed as a Zig package via zig fetch; the EVMC adapter was removed in August 2026 (#33) and the native C API is experimental, so it is not a drop-in EVMC VM for clients that load evmone. The same block validator also builds as an RV64 guest for SP1, ZisK and OpenVM.
how_it_is_fast: Tail-call threaded dispatch: each opcode handler takes the instruction pointer, stack pointer and gas as register arguments, charges gas, executes and jumps to the next handler with @call(.always_tail) (src/interpreter/tail_dispatch.zig), so there is no central loop or per-op capability check. Fork rules, tracing and single-stepping are comptime choices that produce separate specialized dispatch tables, jump validity comes from a precomputed JUMPDEST bitmask, and the executor uses preallocated pooled frames, stacks and buffers. The host interface also offers fused loadStorage/storeStorage callbacks that return access warmth and value in one call, which the benchmark host implements with a single hash-map getOrPut.
when_to_use: A Zig codebase that needs an embeddable EVM interpreter and can track a pre-1.0 API pinned to a commit.
Specialized or custom-fork EVMs (L2 rule changes, extra precompiles, custom opcodes) where compile-time specialization via Spec.extend beats runtime switches.
zkVM guest work: the same stateless block validator compiles for SP1, ZisK and OpenVM with bounded pools.
Compute-heavy contract execution (the snailtracer row: 19.97 ms vs evmone-baseline 59.80 ms on M1, 33.35 vs 57.98 ms on the AMD run), if you can re-measure on your own hardware first.
when_not_to_use: Production consensus or anything handling value: version 0.0.0, unaudited, public API changes between commits, 3 stars and no external users documented.
C/C++ or Rust clients wanting a drop-in for evmone or revm: there is no EVMC adapter any more and only an experimental C API.

Workloads dominated by MSTORE, LOG or many small Keccak calls: evmone-baseline is faster on the M1 MSTORE loop (0.67x), LOG0 rows (0.58x and 0.69x), LOG4 0-byte (0.80x) and ten-thousand-hashes (0.86x).

x86-64 servers if you expect the M1 margins: the older AMD EPYC Genoa run is within about 7% of evmone-baseline on 9 of 14 rows and only clearly ahead on snailtracer (1.74x), SSTORE (1.41x) and MSTORE (1.44x).
Teams that cannot follow Zig toolchain churn: main requires Zig 0.16.x and each release supports one Zig minor.

integration.dependencies: none for the pure-Zig core codecs (rlp, mpt, ssz with .core = false); the EVM core pulls lazy C dependencies for crypto: libsecp256k1 v0.8.0 (default since #69), blst, mcl, and optional XKCP Keccak
integration.min_toolchain: Zig 0.16.0 (minimum_zig_version in build.zig.zon); main tracks Zig 0.16.x
integration.platforms: native x86-64 and aarch64 (benchmarked on Linux x86-64 and macOS arm64); RV64 guest builds for SP1, ZisK, OpenVM

gotchas: Harness flaw in the storage rows: the evmone runner's mock host (bench/evmone/vm_loop.cpp) stores slots in a std::map (red-black tree keyed by a 52-byte array) and every SLOAD/SSTORE goes through two EVMC callbacks (access_storage, then get_storage or set_storage), while evmz's mock host (bench/src/common.zig) uses a Zig AutoHashMap with fused loadStorage/storeStorage callbacks that do one getOrPut; revm's sidecar uses Rust's SipHash HashMap. The storage-sload-loop fixture is 1000 iterations of 8 SLOADs of slot 0, so the 3.97x SLOAD and 5.27x SSTORE wins over evmone-baseline (and part of the ERC20 margins) measure mock-host data structures and callback count as much as the interpreter, unlike the arithmetic loop where the engines are at parity (1.05x).

The published M1 table (dated 2026-08-13, unchanged in bench/README.md since commit d8f5e95) was produced by a harness that pinned evmone at commit 786c96f1 (0.23.0-dev) and revm =41.0.0; PR #65 (2026-09-10) moved the harness to evmone v0.23.0 and revm =43.0.2 without refreshing the tables, so the baseline versions the repo now names are not the ones measured.

Compiler asymmetry: evmone and intx are compiled inside the Zig build by Zig's bundled clang, and Zig passes -O2 (not -O3) for C/C++ sources in ReleaseFast while Zig code gets its -O3 equivalent; evmone's own CMake Release build would use CMake's -O3 default. The M1 run also gives evmz the optional XKCP Keccak while evmone uses its bundled keccak.c.

Cross-engine correctness is not checked: each runner only requires a success status, and compare.zig never compares return data, gas used or logs between engines (EEST conformance runs in CI cover evmz's semantics separately).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick evmz over evmone or revm only when you are in Zig, want compile-time fork specialization or zkVM guest builds, and accept pre-release risk; evmone remains the mature C++ interpreter with an EVMC ABI and revm the Rust incumbent with a large user base. Guillotine's catalogued README table shows it at rough parity with evmone on ERC20 rows, so neither newcomer has a clear win over evmone beyond its own first-party runs.
verified_claims_summary: Author-run VM-core benchmark (deployed runtime bytecode called repeatedly, analysis outside the timed window, fixed Osaka, median of five 100-run medians) on an Apple M1 Max with ReleaseFast and XKCP Keccak: evmz beats evmone-baseline 1.05x to 5.27x on 9 of 14 evm-bench-style fixtures (snailtracer 3.00x, ERC20 transfer 1.66x) and loses on 5, and beats revm's raw interpreter on every row; the older AMD EPYC Genoa KVM run is near parity with evmone-baseline except snailtracer 1.74x. The baselines were evmone 0.23.0-dev built by Zig's clang at -O2 and revm 41.0.0 with fat LTO, and the storage rows are skewed by differing mock hosts.
status_note: Actively developed (last commit 2026-10-05, 174 commits, 0 issues filed) and dual MIT OR Apache-2.0, but pre-release version 0.0.0 with an unstable API, AI-assisted development (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) and only first-party benchmarks whose published tables lag the current harness.
